candidates.name: recsyschallenge/2019
candidates.what_it_holds: Official problem-definition repo for the ACM RecSys Challenge 2019, run by trivago (a hotel metasearch engine that federates Google Hotel Ads-style listings across OTAs). Points to the actual dataset at https://recsys.trivago.cloud/ (registration required to download). The dataset itself (per publicly documented facts about this well-known challenge) is user click-stream session logs from trivago.com in Nov 2018 — each 'clickout' action carries a parallel list of hotel/accommodation impressions and their displayed prices, i.e. a real hotel metasearch price panel, across multiple European + a few non-European platforms/locales, ~900k+ sessions / ~15M+ actions in the full training set.
candidates.why_useful: This is a genuine hotel-metasearch price panel (impressions + prices shown to real users), the closest thing on GitHub to a Google Hotel Ads-style dataset, and speaks to gap #9 (competitor/adjacent supply pricing) and #2 (realised pricing for lodging, ex-Airbnb) as a comparator series for hotel ADR movement around the same period a stay might substitute to/from Airbnb. One-time snapshot (Nov 2018), not continuous or point-in-time vintaged, and requires free registration to pull the actual files — not a plain git-committed dataset.
candidates.geography: Europe-heavy (DE, UK, FR, IT, etc.) plus some US/other trivago markets
candidates.size_hint: ~900k+ sessions, ~15M+ logged actions (documented scale of this well-known challenge; not independently re-verified this session)
candidates.license: Research-use license per trivago's challenge terms; registration required
candidates.last_activity: repo largely static since 2019 challenge close

candidates.name: MaurizioFD/recsys-challenge-2019-trivago
candidates.what_it_holds: Politecnico di Milano team's full solution code/notebooks for the RecSys Challenge 2019 (Policloud8), including preprocessing scripts that read the trivago dataset (train.csv/test.csv/item_metadata.csv style files) in full/local/small (100k-row) modes. No raw data committed (dataset must still be obtained from trivago), but the preprocessing code documents the exact schema (impression lists + parallel price lists per clickout, per-country feature importance table referencing UK/US/DE/FR/IT etc.).
candidates.why_useful: Turns the trivago metasearch dataset into something immediately usable — schema, cleaning, feature engineering already written — if the team decides to pull the underlying trivago data as an ex-Airbnb hotel-pricing comparator.
candidates.geography: Europe + a handful of other trivago markets

candidates.name: trivago/recsys-challenge-2019-data-exploration
candidates.what_it_holds: Official trivago repo with R code reproducing the plots from the RecSys Challenge 2019 dataset paper — temporal patterns and action-type frequencies (search, filter, clickout, interaction with image/rating/info) over the challenge period.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the dataset's temporal/behavioral structure (official source) and gives ready-made exploratory code, useful if the team pulls the trivago dataset for the metasearch-pricing comparator described above.

candidates.name: google/hotel-ads-etl-tool
candidates.what_it_holds: Official (but explicitly deprecated/unmaintained) Google repo: a Python + Apache Beam/Dataflow ETL pipeline that pulls 'Hotel Ads API Reports' (Google Hotel Ads performance data: impressions, clicks, bookings by property) into BigQuery. Requires OAuth2 credentials tied to an active Google Hotel Ads / Hotel Center partner account plus a GCP project (Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Dataflow enabled). 9 stars, 7 forks, Python 93.9%/Shell 6.1%.
candidates.why_useful: The most directly on-theme repo found (literally 'hotel ads etl'), and shows what fields the Hotel Ads API historically exposed, but it is gated behind a partner-only Google Hotel Ads account (a hotel/OTA advertiser login), which the team does not have and which is out of scope to acquire. Useful mainly as documentation of what a real Google Hotel Ads price/bid panel looks like, not as a pullable public dataset.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (typical for google org repos; not independently confirmed)

candidates.name: clementreiffers/hotel-scraping
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/Selenium bots scraping four hotel sites — hotels.com, booking.com, trivago.fr, kayak.fr — for name, address, price, star rating, GPS, capacity, room count, one CSV per site. No data committed to the repo; the tool must be run to produce data. French-locale focus (trivago.fr, kayak.fr).
candidates.why_useful: A working, non-Airbnb scraper that explicitly covers two metasearch engines (trivago, Kayak) alongside two OTAs, so if a human decides scraping non-Airbnb metasearch pages is in-bounds, this is a ready template for building a hotel-price comparator panel.

candidates.name: seanbabalala/hotelrate-crawl (hotelrate-mcp)
candidates.what_it_holds: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for live, on-demand hotel price comparison across Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and Google Hotels (Playwright-based real-time crawling with session persistence for the first three; Google Hotels support is real-time-only). No data committed; ships a demo mode returning synthetic data and a live mode that scrapes. README explicitly notes 20-40% price variance for the same room across OTAs.
candidates.why_useful: One of very few repos that names 'Google Hotels' explicitly as a live price source alongside major OTAs; could in principle be adapted (by a human, not run by an agent) into a repeated snapshot panel of Google Hotels-displayed rates for named markets/dates as an ex-Airbnb ADR cross-check.

notes: Hard blocker this run: the shared WebSearch tool budget (200/200) was already exhausted by other scouts before my first query executed, so I could not use WebSearch at all (three queries returned budget-exhausted errors with zero results). I fell back to WebFetch against github.com/search (429 Too Many Requests — GitHub's search UI rate-limits WebFetch's IP), DuckDuckGo (CAPTCHA wall), Bing (returned only generic google.com navigational links, not real SERPs), Ecosia (403), and Marginalia (bot-check page) before finding that search.brave.com/search worked via WebFetch for a handful of queries -- until it too started returning 429s (Retry-After 3600) after ~6 queries, after which every further Brave query failed for the rest of the session. I then leaned on GitHub topics pages (github.com/topics/<tag>) and raw.githubusercontent.com README fetches, which were NOT rate-limited, to verify/expand. Net result: the Google Hotel Ads / metasearch space on GitHub is thin. The one real find is the trivago RecSys Challenge 2019 dataset (a genuine hotel-metasearch impression+price panel, gated behind free registration on trivago's own site, not git-committed) plus its two companion repos. Google's own hotel-ads-etl-tool is deprecated and gated behind a Hotel Ads partner account. Everything else under hotel-price*/hotel-scraper/google-hotels* topics is a zero-star Apify-actor marketing repo or generic OTA scraper with no committed data and no fixed panel — most of these I excluded per the 'no data and no working method' rule; the ones kept are marked low potential and included mainly to document what exists (or doesn't) in this niche. Recommend a follow-up scout re-run this exact theme later with a fresh WebSearch budget and try `gh search repos` variants (blocked for me by modality rules) since Brave/Bing/DDG were all degraded for this session specifically.
